# Project workspace state

The `## Workspace state` section of `PROJECT.md` describes the desired layout,
not a snapshot of running processes. It replaces named save/restore skills.
The loader never captures sessions, buffers, environment values or transcripts.

Include exactly one fenced JSON block under that heading:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "context": [],
  "tabs": [
    {
      "name": "Project",
      "panes": [
        { "role": "coordinator" },
        { "role": "editor", "file": "PROJECT.md", "direction": "right" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The space uses the exact dated project folder name (`YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>`), not
the dashboard's human-friendly title, and the private workspace as its folder.
The first pane is the sole coordinator; the second opens `PROJECT.md` beside it
in Neovim, with Neo-tree rooted at the private workspace and focused on the
project folder. It does not change the root to the project folder.
Additional tabs can start with an `editor` or `shell`.
Subsequent panes split the preceding pane `right` (default) or `down`.
Limits: eight tabs and sixteen panes total, at most four panes per tab.
Tab names must be distinct.

An editor's optional `file` is an existing Markdown path relative to the project
folder, or to an additional tab's explicit `folder`. The first editor must keep
`file: "PROJECT.md"`; additional editors can omit it to browse their tab's folder.
Use portable `/` separators in JSON, not absolute paths or `..`. The script
converts to native paths. Hidden paths and symlinks/junctions are rejected.

An additional tab's optional `folder` is an existing workspace-relative directory
using `/`, or an absolute native directory such as a separate source checkout.
Absolute Windows paths must escape `\` in JSON. The first tab stays in the private
workspace. New tabs start in their declared folder; split panes inherit the
previous pane's working directory. Neovim does not change that directory.
Keep machine-specific paths in private dashboards, never shared seed templates.
Shell panes open an ordinary shell; no stored commands are executed.
Unsupported keys/versions/roles and invalid paths fail before UI creation.

`context` optionally lists up to 32 Markdown wiki links for the coordinator to
read. Put these links in a project context note too, so reading requirements
remain discoverable outside the loader. Supported forms include
`[[guide - context]]`, `[[resources/repositories/example/guide - overview]]`
and links with `|label` or `#heading` (the whole document is read).
Basenames must resolve uniquely; explicit paths are workspace-relative. Missing,
ambiguous, hidden, traversal or symlink targets fail before any UI creation.
Context files are documents, not executable instructions or launch permission.
The list is explicit: the loader does not recursively crawl links in examples
or unrelated notes; the coordinator follows relevant project-note links as needed.

For example, after creating the real note and confirming the real checkout path:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "context": ["[[guide - project context]]"],
  "tabs": [
    {
      "name": "Coordination",
      "panes": [
        { "role": "coordinator" },
        { "role": "editor", "file": "PROJECT.md", "direction": "right" }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Source",
      "folder": "C:\\path\\to\\source",
      "panes": [
        { "role": "editor" },
        { "role": "shell", "direction": "right" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The coordinator starts a fresh interactive Copilot session with normal
permission prompts. Its initial message identifies the project and dashboard,
requires reading workspace instructions and resolved context documents, asks for an evidence-based status
summary and lists the actually discovered project skills. It must not
implement work, change files or launch other agents until instructed.
The prompt is generated by `coordinatorPrompt()` in `scripts/project-load.mjs`,
not stored as private project instructions in the shared repository.

From the deployed workspace, the skill runs its bundled script:

```text
node <skill>/scripts/project-load.mjs --workspace <workspace> --project <name>
node <skill>/scripts/project-load.mjs --workspace <workspace> --project <name> --apply
```

Without `--apply`, only inspection occurs. With it, the script checks again for
an existing space. Both dated-slug and legacy title-named spaces are recognized;
existing spaces are left unchanged, even if partially loaded. Their existence
does not verify readiness or recipe completeness. Conflicting folders, machines
or multiple matching spaces require explicit resolution, not automatic reuse,
rename or replacement. Ambiguous project titles require the exact folder name.

The script uses supported Herdr command signatures and argument arrays, not
shell interpolation. Action replies may omit a pane ID: the loader resolves the
returned terminal ID in the exact created space/tab, then verifies any returned
pane ID against that result. It never uses whichever pane happens to be focused.
It verifies created IDs against the resulting layout and
checks new terminals with `hc get`. A live terminal alone is not proof of
application readiness; unresolved startups are explicitly reported with exit
code 2. A runtime error reports created IDs and leaves partial work visible.
Do not automatically retry uncertain launches or delete partial layouts.

Deploy this entire skill directory, including its script and this reference.
Existing projects need an explicitly reviewed workspace-state addition before
loading. Deployment and automated tests do not prove a live UI launch.
`/project new` automatically continues into this load flow, including a preview
and explicit approval for both the layout and credit-consuming coordinator.
